title: A baseline adult echocardiogram
indication: Characterize chamber size, systolic function and valve flow in an adult with a soft murmur.
summary: The paired apical sections come from one modeled heartbeat. The Doppler panels show the separately prescribed flow for this worked visit.

views.title: Left ventricular contraction
views.caption: The endocardium moves inward and the base moves toward the apex between these two frames. The paired two-chamber view supplies the second diameter for each volume disk.

views.title: Biplane volumes and atrial size
views.caption: Twenty pairs of disk widths across the apical four- and two-chamber contours yield the end-diastolic and end-systolic LV volumes. Atrial size is assessed at ventricular end systole.
views.measurement: LV 118 → 50 mL · EF 58%. LA volume 41 mL · RA area 20.3 cm².

views.title: Right ventricular function
views.caption: Trace the RV endocardial area in the same RV-focused plane at end diastole and end systole.

views.title: Mitral and tricuspid inflow
views.caption: The first peak is early diastolic filling. The smaller late peak accompanies atrial contraction. Separate septal and lateral annular samples in the echo study illustrate relaxation.
views.measurement: Mitral E/A 79/54 cm/s · E/A ratio 1.46. Tricuspid E/A 57/38 cm/s.

views.title: From root to arch
views.caption: Follow the outlet through the root in parasternal long axis. The suprasternal cut provides a second window on the arch and descending thoracic segment.

views.title: Aortic outflow
views.caption: Sample proximal outflow with PW and the valve jet with CW. Both traces have a complete systolic envelope.
views.measurement: LVOT peak 1.02 m/s · aortic peak 1.31 m/s · mean aortic gradient 3.7 mmHg.

views.title: Pulmonary and tricuspid valves
views.caption: The pulmonary outflow and small tricuspid regurgitant jet appear on the same velocity scale. The TR envelope supplies the RV–RA systolic difference.
views.measurement: Pulmonary peak 0.96 m/s · TR peak 2.20 m/s · RV–RA difference 19 mmHg.

views.title: Systemic venous return
views.caption: The subcostal longitudinal detail follows the same IVC site across breathing. Calipers span the lumen perpendicular to its walls.
views.measurement: 17 mm at end expiration → 7 mm on inspiration · 59% collapse.

views.title: Pericardial space
views.caption: Inspect around the ventricles from subcostal and parasternal windows. The detail models apposed pericardial layers without a fluid stripe.

impression: Preserved modeled LV and RV systolic function (EF 58%, RV area change 54%). No significant outflow obstruction in the displayed spectra. No pericardial effusion in the worked survey.
limitations: Sections are cuts through authored anatomy. Flow, respiratory IVC change and the pericardial detail are prescribed illustrations. The companion 17-window exam supplies parasternal, apical, subcostal and suprasternal acquisition context.

title: Aortic stenosis across two Doppler windows
indication: Characterize a systolic ejection murmur in an adult with exertional dyspnea.
summary: In this case the jet is directed toward the right parasternal window. Compare the recorded velocities before integrating the valve, gradient and effective area.

views.title: Valve morphology
views.caption: Inspect the reduced central opening and thickened cusp edges in systole. The mobile-cusp example at left provides an orientation comparison.

views.title: LVOT diameter and flow
views.caption: Place an inner-edge diameter at cusp insertion and sample just proximal to the acceleration zone. Both enter the continuity calculation.

views.title: Compare continuous-wave windows
views.caption: The apical beam samples a lower component of the same jet. The dense right parasternal envelope is complete and reaches a higher peak. The mean gradient averages 4v² over ejection.
views.measurement: Apical 3.59 m/s · right parasternal 4.54 m/s · mean gradient 45 mmHg.

impression: Severe high-gradient aortic stenosis in this modeled visit. The best aligned window yields Vmax 4.54 m/s and mean gradient 45 mmHg. LVOT VTI 18.8 cm ÷ valve VTI 109.4 cm gives a dimensionless ratio of 0.17. Multiplying this ratio by the LVOT area, π × (2.10 cm / 2)², gives an effective valve area of 0.59 cm².
limitations: The valve detail and smooth Doppler envelopes are authored. The comparison in Figure 5 is a separate acquired exam. The schematic valve opening and effective flow area represent different measurements.

title: A murmur with an incomplete jet envelope
indication: Assess suspected valve obstruction when acoustic access is poor.
summary: Valve motion raises suspicion, but the spectral signal drops out near peak ejection. A repeat from the right parasternal window also loses the jet.

views.title: Restricted cusp motion
views.caption: The right-hand valve schematic establishes a structural reason to interrogate the outflow. Morphology alone cannot grade the obstruction.

views.title: Apical acquisition and repeat
views.caption: Both attempted alignments have a gap through the expected peak. The visible shoulders cannot supply a valid peak, mean gradient or valve VTI.

impression: Restricted aortic valve opening. Hemodynamic severity is indeterminate. No reportable maximum velocity, mean gradient or continuity valve area from these acquisitions.
limitations: Further diagnostic imaging would be needed to answer the referral. The missing range is deliberately omitted in both illustrations.
